main_body: Beehive hut: a large conical thatched roof (rows 2-56) over a mud-brick wall with a dark arched doorway (rows 57-78)
top_band: Thatch roof slope from row 2 down to about row 55, in light gold (#d8bb68) and mid ochre bands separated by dark ridge lines. Directly under it is a dark eave shadow row, then the brown wall.
evidence: The roof is a big sloped surface seen from above, with a darker overhanging eave edge at rows 55-58 and a separate vertical mud wall below. The doorway has a frame and dark inner shading, so it reads as inset. The roof and wall are clearly distinct and there is no receding side face. It reads as a 3/4 building in the same way as the reference roofs.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 lightness steps, with horizontal courses and dashed straw ticks, and the outline is a tinted dark brown (only 5% neutral). However, the wall is mostly flat brown with only a few sparse light dashes, and the door interior and the base strip are flat dark areas. The measured facts are 31 distinct colours against 66 and 185 for the references, median 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18, and 12% flat-fill coverage against 0%. That makes it thinner and flatter than the Beodeul references, so it fails on style.
